correctness.rationale: Let f,g be the two mass functions. For any integer z, the convolution at z is an average of f(z-y) against g(y), so it is at most M(B_1), and symmetrically at most M(B_2). Since m→m^(-2)-1 is decreasing, the sum deficit is at least the maximum of the two individual deficits and hence their average. Equality in the average bound requires both deficits equal and the summed maximum atom equal to each individual maximum atom. If one variable is deterministic, equal deficits force the other to be deterministic. Otherwise each Bernoulli gives positive weight to 0 and 1, so equality in the convolution average forces f(z)=f(z-1)=M(B_1) at a maximizing z and symmetrically for g. Thus z=1 and both Bernoulli variables are fair. The fair sum has masses (1/4,1/2,1/4), each of the three deficits is 3, and the ratio is 1/2. The frozen modal-orientation formulas give the same contraction, and their r,s in [0,1] bounds include all degenerate and tied modes. The independent exact replay `python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_math_checks.py` checked 441 parameter pairs on mesh 1/20 and found the four fully deterministic ordered pairs and one fair pair as the only equalities on that grid. The averaging argument proves the full result.
